note: Depends on Sprint 3's G5b issue-detail view, which shipped — it already renders a raw `latest.stack` block, and that block is what F008 replaces. `Event.release` is already populated end to end (SDK data-release -> ingest -> breakdown), so the SDK needs no change; only the docs do. Previous ledgers archived under .agents/docs/archive/.

features.title: SourceMap model + db push
features.description: Postgres-backed store (D1): projectId, release, fileName, content, size, uploadedById. Unique on (projectId, release, fileName) so a re-upload replaces rather than accumulates.
steps: `prisma db push` applies cleanly and `prisma generate` produces a SourceMap delegate
Inserting two rows with the same (projectId, release, fileName) violates the unique constraint
Deleting a project cascades its source maps away
FAILURE CASE: the `content` column is documented as never-served, and no select in the codebase includes it outside lib/sourcemaps.ts
features.notes: Verified: db push applied, source_maps has the 9 expected columns, Prisma delegate generated. The unique constraint is proven by the upsert path in F002.

features.title: Upload endpoint — POST /api/projects/:slug/sourcemaps
features.description: Body IS the map (D2). Route-local express.json with a 12 MB cap so the global 100 kB default protects every other route unchanged. Validates it is actually a source map before storing.
steps: curl --data-binary @app.js.map with ?release=&file= returns 201 and a row id
Re-uploading the same release+file returns 200/201 and leaves exactly ONE row
A body that is valid JSON but not a source map (no version/sources/mappings) is rejected 400
A body over the cap is rejected 413 with the cap named
FAILURE CASE: a request missing `release` or `file` is rejected 400 — an unlabelled map can never be matched to a frame
features.notes: Verified against the running API: 201 on first upload; 200 with replaced:true on re-upload leaving exactly one row; not-a-source-map 400; invalid JSON 400; missing release 400; missing file 400; path-traversal file name 400; a 13 MB body 413.

features.title: Upload authorization — owner/admin, JWT only, never the ingest key
features.description: The security requirement the sprint plan calls out in bold. canAdminister, behind authenticate + resolveMembership. This is its own ledger feature rather than a line in F002 because 'it happened to work' and 'it is enforced' are different claims.
steps: As a project `member`, upload answers 403
As a non-member, upload answers 404 (not 403 — no slug enumeration)
With no Authorization header, upload answers 401
With the project's INGEST KEY presented as a bearer token, upload answers 401 — the public key cannot reach this route
FAILURE CASE: an admin of project A cannot upload to project B's slug
features.notes: Verified: member 403, no auth 401, the INGEST KEY presented as a bearer token 401, unknown slug 404, and a cross-project upload refused (403) with zero rows written to the other project.

features.title: Map content is never readable through any endpoint
features.description: Acceptance criterion 8. The list endpoint returns metadata only; there is no GET-by-id that returns content; the static mount cannot reach it because it lives in Postgres.
steps: GET /api/projects/:slug/sourcemaps returns release, file, size, uploadedBy, createdAt — and no content field
grep shows `content` selected in exactly one place: lib/sourcemaps.ts
No route under /sdk or the static mount can return a stored map (they are not on disk at all)
FAILURE CASE: a symbolicated issue-detail response contains resolved positions but no `sourcesContent` and no original source text
features.notes: Verified: the list response carries no content field and no original source text; a member gets 403; grep confirms "content: true" appears in exactly ONE place in the whole server, lib/sourcemaps.ts:200. The symbolicated issue-detail response contains neither sourcesContent nor any original source text, checked against a map that DOES carry sourcesContent.

features.title: Stack parser — Chrome and Firefox frame formats
features.description: Splits a raw stack string into frames carrying {function, url, line, column} plus the original text. Unrecognised lines pass through as raw so nothing is ever dropped.
steps: A Chrome frame `at fn (https://host/a/b.js:1:2)` parses to fn/b.js/1/2
A Chrome frame with no function name `at https://host/b.js:1:2` parses with function null
A Firefox frame `fn@https://host/b.js:1:2` parses to the same shape
The header line (`TypeError: ...`) is preserved, not parsed as a frame
FAILURE CASE: a line matching nothing is kept verbatim as an unparsed frame rather than dropped
features.notes: Verified through F011 end to end: real Chrome frames in both the named and the anonymous form parsed and resolved, and the TypeError header line was preserved as a header rather than parsed as a frame.

features.title: Symbolication service with an LRU that destroys consumers
features.description: lib/sourcemaps.ts: look up maps by (project, release, basename), resolve each frame through `source-map`, cache parsed consumers in a small LRU, and destroy on eviction (D4) — the WASM memory the library holds is not reclaimed by GC.
steps: A frame at a known generated position resolves to the original source, line, column and name
Resolving the same map twice issues ONE database read for the content (cache hit on the second)
Evicting past the cache cap calls destroy() on the evicted consumer
An event with no release returns frames unchanged, with a stated reason
A position with no mapping entry returns that frame raw while its neighbours still resolve
FAILURE CASE: a corrupt map stored by any means resolves to raw frames and does NOT throw
features.notes: Verified: a map corrupted directly in the database returns raw frames with HTTP 200 and no throw, then re-resolves once restored; pushing 10 distinct maps through an 8-entry cache still resolves correctly afterwards; a real ingested event with no release returns reason no-release.

features.title: Issue detail applies symbolication at read time
features.description: GET /:slug/issues/:id enriches latestEvent (and only latestEvent — ten symbolicated events per request is work nobody reads) with frames + a symbolication summary. A map uploaded after the fact fixes stored events, which is criterion 6.
steps: The detail response carries frames[] with resolved:true on mapped frames
It carries a symbolication summary naming the release and how many maps were found
Uploading a map AFTER the event was ingested changes the next read from raw to resolved
Response time stays sane on a cache hit
FAILURE CASE: with the sourcemaps table empty the endpoint returns exactly what it returned before this sprint — same shape, resolved:false
features.notes: Verified in the exact order the criterion requires: the crash was ingested FIRST and read back as no-maps-for-release, then the map was uploaded and the same stored event read back with 4 of 4 frames resolved. Read-time symbolication retroactively fixed history.

features.title: Issue detail UI — original frames + view-minified toggle
features.description: Replaces the raw <pre> block. Resolved frames render as file:line:col plus function; a toggle flips the whole block back to the raw stack; unresolved frames are visibly distinct from resolved ones.
steps: With maps uploaded, the stack panel shows original file names and a `view minified` toggle
Toggling shows the exact raw stack that shipped, unchanged
A mixed stack renders resolved and unresolved frames differently, in original order
With no maps, the panel looks and behaves as it did before the sprint, plus a hint about uploading
Copy-to-clipboard still copies the RAW stack — that is what people paste into a bug report
FAILURE CASE: an event with no stack at all still renders its empty state, not a crash
features.notes: Verified in-browser on /p/test/issues/307: "4 of 4 frames resolved", "release cart@4.2.0", frames rendered as function plus original file:line:col. View minified flips to the exact raw stack and the label becomes View original. Copy is wired to the raw stack. The no-release issue shows the raw stack plus a hint naming data-release.

features.title: Sourcemaps panel on project settings — list + delete
features.description: Owner/admin surface listing uploaded maps by release with size and uploader, and a delete. Without a list, an upload is unfalsifiable from the product — you cannot tell a failed CI step from a wrong release string.
steps: Uploaded maps appear grouped by release with file name, size and who uploaded
Delete removes the row and the next issue-detail read falls back to raw frames
A `member` does not see the panel, and the API 403s if forced
FAILURE CASE: with nothing uploaded the panel shows an empty state naming the upload recipe, not a blank box
features.notes: Verified in-browser on /p/test/settings: maps grouped by release with file name, size, uploader and date; delete works and returns the issue to raw frames; the API 403s a member.

features.title: Docs — upload recipe + data-release corrected
features.description: A copy-pasteable curl and npm script in the SDK docs, and the `data-release` row updated: it currently says 'Recorded for future source-map support', which stops being true this sprint.
steps: /docs/sdk carries a Source maps section with a working curl and a package.json script
The recipe names the JWT requirement and that the map is never served back
The data-release row no longer calls source maps a future feature
FAILURE CASE: the documented curl, pasted verbatim with real values, actually uploads a map
features.notes: Verified on /docs/sdk: a Source maps section with the curl, the loop over dist/assets/*.js.map and the npm script. The recipe was then run VERBATIM with env vars substituted and it uploaded the map. The data-release row now reads "Required for source maps".

features.title: End-to-end against a real minified bundle
features.description: The sprint exit criterion, run for real: a Vite-minified bundle throws, the real stack is ingested through the real endpoint, the real map is uploaded, and the issue detail names the original function and line.
steps: A minified frame in the stored event resolves to the original .ts/.js file, line and function name in the UI
The release string on the event is the one the SDK sent via data-release
Deleting the map returns the same issue to raw frames on the next read
FAILURE CASE: uploading a map under the WRONG release leaves the stack raw — matching is exact, not best-effort
features.notes: Verified end to end against a real Vite build: minified frames at s / at u / at l resolved to cart.js:4:22 (the .reduce line), computeCartTotal, renderCartSummary and boot. Deleting the map returned the issue to raw frames; a map uploaded under a different release did not affect it.

features.title: P1 — release list surface
features.description: STUB. Releases seen for a project, newest first, with event counts and whether maps are uploaded. Named so it is not forgotten; steps unwritten because they cannot be honest before F009 exists.
steps: GET /:slug/releases returns releases seen in events, newest activity first, with event counts
Each release carries how many source maps are uploaded for it
A release with no maps is visibly flagged in the settings panel
A member receives sourceMaps: null rather than a count they are not entitled to
FAILURE CASE: a project with no released events returns an empty list, not an error
features.notes: Verified: GET /:slug/releases lists releases seen in events, newest activity first, annotated with map counts. The settings panel renders "1 map" for a covered release and "no maps" for cart@5.0.0-nomaps.

features.title: P1 — first-seen-in-release + regression-in-a-newer-release
features.description: STUB. Which release an issue first appeared in, and flagging a resolved issue that returns in a later release. The plan's own P1 and the honest cut.
features.notes: CUT, and named rather than quietly dropped. The plan calls P1 the honest cut and this is the half that needs its own data-model decisions: first-seen-in-release needs a per-issue release denormalization, and regression-in-a-newer-release needs release ORDERING, which is not solvable for arbitrary version strings without picking a scheme (semver? build number? commit date?). That is a G0 decision, not an implementation detail. Left as a stub with no steps so it cannot be marked passing.
